style="height:27pt"><td colspan="3" style="border-bottom:1pt solid #001871;padding:0 1pt"><div><span><br/></span></div></td></tr></table></div><div style="margin-bottom:12pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:108%">Enterprise Risk Management</span></div><div id="i279937ea94ee4eff90367a37e7220900_253"></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">Risk management is an integral part of our business strategy and a key element of our approach to corporate governance. We have an integrated process for managing risks throughout our organization in accordance with our firm-wide risk appetite. Our Board of Directors has oversight responsibility for the management of risk. Our Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Department oversees and integrates the risk management functions in our business and embeds risk management in our day-to-day business processes, providing senior management with a consolidated view of AIG&#8217;s major risk positions. Nevertheless, our risk management efforts may not always be successful and material adverse effects on our business, results of operations, cash flows, liquidity or financial condition may occur. </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">For further information regarding the risks associated with our business and operations, see</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%"> </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors in the 2025 Annual Report.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">AIG employs a Three Lines model. AIG&#8217;s business leaders assume full accountability for the risks and controls in their segments and functions, and ERM and other second line functions have review, challenge and oversight function. The third line consists of our Internal Audit Group that provides independent assurance to AIG&#8217;s Board of Directors.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">For additional information on AIG&#8217;s risk management program, see Part II, Item 7. MD&amp;A &#9472; Enterprise Risk Management in the 2025 Annual Report.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">The scope and magnitude of our market risk exposures is managed under a robust framework that contains defined risk limits and minimum standards for managing market risk in a manner consistent with our risk appetite statement.</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:133%"> </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">As of March 31, 2026, there have been no material changes in our market risk exposures, which may be found in </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">Part II, Item 7. MD&amp;A &#9472; Enterprise Risk Management in the 2025 Annual Report. See Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors in the 2025 Annual Report on how difficult conditions in the financial markets and the economy generally may materially adversely affect our business and results of our operations.</span></div><div style="height:43.2pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-align:right;text-indent:36pt"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:34.769%"><tr><td style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;text-decoration:underline" href="#i279937ea94ee4eff90367a37e7220900_7">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></span></div><div style="padding-left:360pt;text-align:right"><span><br/></span></div><div style="text-align:right"><span style="color:#1252de;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Glossary</span></div><div style="text-align:right"><span><br/></span></div></div><div><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:99.943%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:98.900%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/></tr><tr style="height:27pt"><td colspan="3" style="border-bottom:1pt solid #001871;padding:0 1pt"><div><span><br/></span></div></td></tr></table></div><div style="margin-bottom:12pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:108%">Glossary</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Accident year  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The annual calendar accounting period in which loss events occurred, regardless of when the losses are actually reported, booked or paid.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Accident year combined ratio, as adjusted (Accident year combined ratio, ex-CAT)  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The combined ratio excluding catastrophe losses and related reinstatement premiums, net of reinsurance, and prior year development, net of prior year premiums, net of reinsurance, and the impact of reserve discounting.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Accident year loss ratio, as adjusted (Accident year loss ratio, ex-CAT)  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The loss ratio excluding catastrophe losses and related reinstatement premiums, net of reinsurance, and prior year development, net of prior year premiums, net of reinsurance, and the impact of reserve discounting.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Acquisition ratio  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Acquisition costs divided by net premiums earned. Acquisition costs are those costs incurred to acquire new and renewal insurance contracts and also include the amortization of VOBA and DAC. Acquisition costs vary with sales and include, but are not limited to, commissions, premium taxes, direct marketing costs and certain costs of personnel engaged in sales support activities such as underwriting.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Attritional losses </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">are losses recorded in the current accident year, which are not catastrophe losses.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Book value per share, excluding Investments AOCI, deferred tax assets (DTA) and AIG&#8217;s ownership interest in Corebridge (Core operating book value per share)</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> is used to show the amount of our net worth on a per share basis after eliminating Investments AOCI, DTA and AIG&#8217;s ownership interest in Corebridge. We believe this measure is useful to investors because it eliminates the fair value of investments that can fluctuate significantly from period to period due to changes in market conditions. We also exclude the portion of DTA representing U.S. tax attributes related to net operating loss carryforwards (NOLs), corporate alternative minimum tax credits (CAMTCs) and foreign tax credits (FTCs) that have not yet been utilized. Amounts for interim periods are estimates based on projections of full-year attribute utilization. As NOLs, CAMTCs and FTCs are utilized, the corresponding portion of the DTA utilized is included. We exclude AIG&#8217;s ownership interest in Corebridge since it is not a core long-term investment for AIG. Core operating book value per share is derived by dividing total AIG common shareholders&#8217; equity, excluding Investments AOCI, DTA and AIG&#8217;s ownership interest in Corebridge (AIG core operating shareholders&#8217; equity) by total common shares outstanding. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Book value per share, excluding investments related cumulative unrealized gains and losses recorded in Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) (AOCI) adjusted for the cumulative unrealized gains and losses related to Fortitude Re funds withheld assets (collectively, Investments AOCI) (Adjusted book value per share)</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> is used to show the amount of our net worth on a per share basis after eliminating the fair value of investments that can fluctuate significantly from period to period due to changes in market conditions. In addition, we adjust for the cumulative unrealized gains and losses related to Fortitude Re funds withheld assets since these fair value movements are economically transferred to Fortitude Re. Adjusted book value per share is derived by dividing total AIG common shareholders&#8217; equity, excluding Investments AOCI (AIG adjusted common shareholders' equity) by total common shares outstanding.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Casualty insurance  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Insurance that is primarily associated with the losses caused by injuries to third persons, i.e., not the insured, and the legal liability imposed on the insured as a result.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Combined ratio  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Sum of the loss ratio and the acquisition and general operating expense ratios.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Credit Support Annex</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">A legal document generally associated with an ISDA Master Agreement that provides for collateral postings which could vary depending on ratings and threshold levels.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">DAC  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Deferred Policy Acquisition Costs  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Deferred costs that are incremental and directly related to the successful acquisition of new business or renewal of existing business.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Deferred gain on retroactive reinsurance  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Retroactive reinsurance is a reinsurance contract in which an assuming entity agrees to reimburse a ceding entity for liabilities incurred as a result of past insurable events. If the amount of premium paid by the ceding reinsurer is less than the related ceded loss reserves, the resulting gain is deferred and amortized over the settlement period of the reserves. Any related development on the ceded loss reserves recoverable under the contract would increase the deferred gain if unfavorable, or decrease the deferred gain if favorable.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Expense ratio  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Sum of acquisition expenses and general operating expenses, divided by net premiums earned.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">General operating expense ratio  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">General operating expenses divided by net premiums earned. General operating expenses are those costs that are generally attributed to the support infrastructure of the organization and include but are not limited to personnel costs, projects and bad debt expenses. General operating expenses exclude losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, acquisition expenses, and investment expenses.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">IBNR  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Incurred But Not Reported  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Estimates of claims that have been incurred but not reported to us.</span></div><div style="height:43.2pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:34.769%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:17.928%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/><td style="color:#1252de;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Glossary</span></div><div style="text-align:right"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">ISDA Master Agreement  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">An agreement between two counterparties, which may have multiple derivative transactions with each other governed by such agreement, that generally provides for the net settlement of all or a specified group of these derivative transactions, as well as pledged collateral, through a single payment, in a single currency, in the event of a default on, or affecting any, one derivative transaction or a termination event affecting all, or a specified group of, derivative transactions.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loan-to-value ratio  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Principal amount of loan amount divided by appraised value of collateral securing the loan.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loss Adjustment Expenses</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The expenses directly attributed to settling and paying claims of insureds and include, but are not limited to, legal fees, adjuster&#8217;s fees and the portion of general expenses allocated to claim settlement costs.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loss ratio  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred divided by net premiums earned.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loss reserve development  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The increase or decrease in incurred losses and loss adjustment expenses related to prior years as a result of the re-estimation of loss reserves at successive valuation dates for a given group of claims.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loss reserves  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Liability for unpaid losses and loss adjustment expenses. The estimated ultimate cost of settling claims relating to insured events that have occurred on or before the balance sheet date, whether or not reported to the insurer at that date.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Master netting agreement  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">An agreement between two counterparties who have multiple derivative contracts with each other that provides for the net settlement of all contracts covered by such agreement, as well as pledged collateral, through a single payment, in a single currency, in the event of default on or upon termination of any one such contract.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Natural catastrophe losses </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">are generally weather or seismic events having a net impact on AIG in excess of $10 million each and man-made catastrophe losses, such as terrorism and civil unrest that exceed the $10 million threshold.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Net premiums written </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">represent the sales of an insurer, adjusted for reinsurance premiums assumed and ceded, during a given period. Net premiums earned are the revenue of an insurer for covering risk during a given period. Net premiums written are a measure of performance for a sales period, while net premiums earned are a measure of performance for a coverage period.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Noncontrolling interests  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The portion of equity ownership in a consolidated subsidiary not attributable to the controlling parent company.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Pool  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">A reinsurance arrangement whereby all of the underwriting results of the pool members are combined and then shared by each member in accordance with its pool participation percentage.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Prior year development  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">See Loss reserve development</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Reinstatement premiums  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Premiums on an insurance policy over and above the initial premium imposed at the beginning of the policy payable to reinsurers or receivable from insurers to restore coverage limits that have been reduced or exhausted as a result of reinsured losses under certain excess of loss reinsurance contracts.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Reinsurance  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The practice whereby one insurer, the reinsurer, in consideration of a premium paid to that insurer, agrees to indemnify another insurer, the ceding company, for part or all of the liability of the ceding company under one or more policies or contracts of insurance which it has issued.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Reinsurance recoverables</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> are comprised of paid losses recoverable, ceded loss reserves, ceded reserves for unearned premiums.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Retroactive reinsurance  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">See Deferred gain on retroactive reinsurance</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Return on equity &#8211; Adjusted after-tax income excluding Investments AOCI (Adjusted return on equity)</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> is used to show the rate of return on common shareholders&#8217; equity excluding Investments AOCI. We believe this measure is useful to investors because it eliminates the fair value of investments which can fluctuate significantly from period to period due to changes in market conditions. Adjusted return on equity is derived by dividing actual or, for interim periods, annualized adjusted after-tax income attributable to AIG common shareholders by average AIG adjusted common shareholders&#8217; equity.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001871;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Return on equity &#8211; Adjusted after-tax income excluding Investments AOCI, DTA and AIG&#8217;s ownership interest in Corebridge (Core operating return on equity) </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">is used to show the rate of return on common shareholders&#8217; equity excluding Investments AOCI, DTA and AIG&#8217;s ownership interest in Corebridge. We believe this measure is useful to investors because it eliminates the fair value of investments that can fluctuate significantly from period to period due to changes in market conditions. We also exclude the portion of DTA representing U.S. tax attributes related to NOLs, CAMTCs and FTCs that have not yet been utilized. Amounts for interim periods are estimates based on projections of full-year attribute utilization. As NOLs, CAMTCs and FTCs are utilized, the corresponding portion of the DTA utilized is included. We exclude AIG&#8217;s ownership interest in Corebridge since it is not a core long-term investment for AIG. We believe this metric provides investors with greater insight as to the underlying profitability of our property and casualty business. Core operating return on equity is derived by dividing actual or, for interim periods, annualized adjusted after-tax income attributable to AIG common shareholders by average AIG core operating shareholders&#8217; equity. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:133%">Subrogation  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">The amount of recovery for claims we have paid our policyholders, generally from a negligent third party or such party&#8217;s insurer.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Unearned premium reserve  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Liabilities established by insurers and reinsurers to reflect unearned premiums, which are usually refundable to policyholders if an insurance or reinsurance contract is canceled prior to expiration of the contract term.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><span style="color:#001770;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">VOBA  </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Value of Business Acquired </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Present value of future pre-tax profits from in-force policies of acquired businesses discounted at yields applicable at the time of purchase. VOBA is reported in DAC in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets.</span></div><div style="height:43.2pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div
